passages.text: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph.
passages.sermon: This psalm is for the choirmaster.\r\nJeduthun will direct the music.\r\nAsaph wrote this psalm.

passages.text: I cried out to God; I cried aloud to God to hear me.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He gave instructions for Jeduthun.
I cried out to God.
I raised my voice to God.
I wanted God to hear me.
passages.original: לַמְנַצֵּ֥חַ עַֽל־ יְדִיתוּן לְאָסָ֥ף מִזְמֽוֹר׃ קוֹלִ֣י אֶל־ אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאֶצְעָ֑קָה קוֹלִ֥י אֶל־ אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים וְהַאֲזִ֥ין אֵלָֽי׃

passages.text: In the day of trouble I sought the Lord; through the night my outstretched hands did not grow weary; my soul refused to be comforted.
passages.sermon:
Asaph wrote this psalm.
He spoke to the Lord.
He faced a day of trouble.
He sought the Lord during his trouble.
He stretched out his hands to God at night.
He did not stop reaching out.
His soul refused comfort.
passages.original: בְּי֥וֹם צָרָתִי֮ אֲדֹנָ֪י דָּ֫רָ֥שְׁתִּי יָדִ֤י׀ לַ֣יְלָה נִ֭גְּרָה וְלֹ֣א תָפ֑וּג מֵאֲנָ֖ה הִנָּחֵ֣ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: I remembered You, O God, and I groaned; I mused and my spirit grew faint. Selah You have kept my eyes from closing; I am too troubled to speak.
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to God.
The psalmist remembers God.
The psalmist groans.
The psalmist thinks deeply.
The psalmist’s spirit grows weak.
God keeps the psalmist’s eyes open.
The psalmist cannot sleep.
The psalmist feels overwhelmed.
The psalmist cannot speak.
passages.original: אֶזְכְּרָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאֶֽהֱמָיָ֑ה אָשִׂ֓יחָה׀ וְתִתְעַטֵּ֖ף רוּחִ֣י סֶֽלָה׃ אָ֭חַזְתָּ שְׁמֻר֣וֹת עֵינָ֑י נִ֝פְעַ֗מְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אֲדַבֵּֽר׃

passages.text: I considered the days of old, the years long in the past.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a person in distress.
The speaker thinks about the past.
The speaker remembers days from long ago.
The speaker remembers years from ancient times.

passages.text: At night I remembered my song; in my heart I mused, and my spirit pondered: “Will the Lord spurn us forever and never show His favor again?
passages.sermon:
The psalmist speaks to God.
The psalmist feels deep distress.
At night, the psalmist remembers his song.
He thinks about God in his heart.
He reflects quietly within himself.
His spirit searches for answers.
He asks a question about God.
He wonders if the Lord will reject His people forever.
He asks if God will ever show favor again.
passages.original: אֶֽזְכְּרָ֥ה נְגִינָתִ֗י בַּ֫לָּ֥יְלָה עִם־ לְבָבִ֥י אָשִׂ֑יחָה וַיְחַפֵּ֥שׂ רוּחִֽי׃ הַֽ֭לְעוֹלָמִים יִזְנַ֥ח׀ אֲדֹנָ֑י וְלֹֽא־ יֹסִ֖יף לִרְצ֣וֹת עֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Is His loving devotion gone forever? Has His promise failed for all time?
passages.sermon:
God is loving and faithful.
I ask a question about God.
Is His loving devotion gone forever?
Has His promise ended for every generation?
passages.original: הֶאָפֵ֣ס לָנֶ֣צַח חַסְדּ֑וֹ גָּ֥מַר אֹ֝֗מֶר לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃

passages.text: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has His anger shut off His compassion?” Selah So I said, “I am grieved that the right hand of the Most High has changed.”
passages.sermon:
God is gracious.
God shows compassion.
I ask, has God forgotten to be gracious?
I ask, has God in His anger shut off His compassion?
I pause and reflect.
I feel deep sorrow.
I say, I am grieved.
I see that the right hand of the Most High has changed.
passages.original: הֲשָׁכַ֣ח חַנּ֣וֹת אֵ֑ל אִם־ קָפַ֥ץ בְּ֝אַ֗ף רַחֲמָ֥יו סֶֽלָה׃ וָ֭אֹמַר חַלּ֣וֹתִי הִ֑יא שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת יְמִ֣ין עֶלְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: I will remember the works of the LORD; yes, I will remember Your wonders of old.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a person who trusts God.
The speaker chooses to remember what the LORD has done.
The speaker remembers the works of the LORD.
The speaker also remembers the wonders God did long ago.
God did great and amazing things in the past.
The speaker thinks about these wonders from old times.
passages.original: אַזְכִּיר מַֽעַלְלֵי־ יָ֑הּ כִּֽי־ אֶזְכְּרָ֖ה מִקֶּ֣דֶם פִּלְאֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: I will reflect on all You have done and ponder Your mighty deeds.
passages.sermon: I will think about everything You have done.\r\nI will speak about Your powerful works.\r\n

passages.text: Your way, O God, is holy. What god is so great as our God?
passages.sermon:
God is holy.
God’s way is holy.
No other god is as great as our God.
Our God is greater than all others.
passages.original: אֱ֭לֹהִים בַּקֹּ֣דֶשׁ דַּרְכֶּ֑ךָ מִי־ אֵ֥ל גָּ֝ד֗וֹל כֵּֽאלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: You are the God who works wonders; You display Your strength among the peoples.
passages.sermon:
God works wonders.
God shows His power to all nations.
God is mighty.
God reveals His strength to everyone.
passages.original: אַתָּ֣ה הָ֭אֵל עֹ֣שֵׂה פֶ֑לֶא הוֹדַ֖עְתָּ בָעַמִּ֣ים עֻזֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: With power You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and swirled; even the depths were shaken.
passages.sermon:
God is powerful.
God redeemed His people with strength.
God saved the sons of Jacob and Joseph.
The waters saw God.
The waters trembled when they saw God.
The depths shook because of God.
passages.original: גָּאַ֣לְתָּ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ עַמֶּ֑ךָ בְּנֵי־ יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְיוֹסֵ֣ף סֶֽלָה׃ רָ֘א֤וּךָ מַּ֨יִם׀ אֱ‍ֽלֹהִ֗ים רָא֣וּךָ מַּ֣יִם יָחִ֑ילוּ אַ֝֗ף יִרְגְּז֥וּ תְהֹמֽוֹת׃

passages.text: The clouds poured down water; the skies resounded with thunder; Your arrows flashed back and forth.
passages.sermon:
God controls the skies and the weather.
Clouds poured down water.
The skies made a loud sound like thunder.
God’s arrows flashed back and forth in the sky.
These arrows are lightning.
passages.original: זֹ֤רְמוּ מַ֨יִם׀ עָב֗וֹת ק֭וֹל נָתְנ֣וּ שְׁחָקִ֑ים אַף־ חֲ֝צָצֶ֗יךָ יִתְהַלָּֽכוּ׃

passages.text: Your thunder resounded in the whirlwind; the lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and quaked.
passages.sermon:
God showed His power.
God’s thunder sounded in the whirlwind.
God’s lightning lit up the whole world.
The earth trembled.
The earth shook.
passages.original: ק֤וֹל רַעַמְךָ֨׀ בַּגַּלְגַּ֗ל הֵאִ֣ירוּ בְרָקִ֣ים תֵּבֵ֑ל רָגְזָ֖ה וַתִּרְעַ֣שׁ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Your path led through the sea, Your way through the mighty waters, but Your footprints were not to be found.
passages.sermon:
God led His people through the sea.
God made a way through the mighty waters.
No one could see God's footprints.
God's presence was real, but His steps were hidden.
passages.original: בַּיָּ֤ם דַּרְכֶּ֗ךָ וּשְׁבִילֶיךָ בְּמַ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝עִקְּבוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א נֹדָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
passages.sermon:
God led His people.
He guided them like a shepherd leads a flock.
God used Moses and Aaron to lead His people.
Moses and Aaron acted by God's direction.
God's people followed Moses and Aaron.
passages.original: נָחִ֣יתָ כַצֹּ֣אן עַמֶּ֑ךָ בְּֽיַד־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאַהֲרֹֽן׃
